dct_description_sm: Research on the ecology and toxicology of tundra peregrine falcons (Falco peregrinus tundrius) has been conducted at Rankin Inlet, Nunavut since 1980.  The population was largely unknown until 1980, when preliminary work indicated a very dense and productive population. Research was motivated initially by the need to understand processes responsible for a worldwide decline in peregrine falcon populations, most notably those caused by widespread DDT contamination. However, the population at Rankin Inlet also provided a unique opportunity for studying the basic biology of the species. To develop a long-term monitoring program for peregrine falcons of basic demography (occupancy, reproductive success, recruitment and survival), raptor ecology (migration, diet, home range size and overlap), and examine these components in the context of climate change and industrial development.
dct_title_s: Biology and Toxicology of Peregrine Falcons in Igloolik, Nunavut
